correctness.rationale: For any putative positive-finite-mean stationary law the arrival rate λ=1−p₀ is positive and less than one: at λ=1 every finite state can hit zero via successive empty arrivals, so a stationary law cannot have p₀=0. For fixed 0<λ<1, negative unit-service drift off zero and irreducibility give a unique queue invariant law, with moments from geometric drift. In fact P(z)=(1−λ)exp(λ(z−1))/(1−∫₀^λ exp(s(z−1))ds), giving a compound-geometric factor and validating its evaluation at two for λ=2−√2, since e^λ−1<1. Stationarity requires p₀=1−λ. Expanding the PGF at one gives m=λ+λ²/[2(1−λ)] and Var=m+[λ²/(2(1−λ))]²+λ³/[3(1−λ)], with mean a bijection onto (0,∞) and variance 4/3 at mean one. The squared-survival identity with independent copies gives G(X)≤1−(2−√2)²<2/3, while the mean-one geometric law gives exactly 2/3. The independent PGF-convolution replay using outward-rounded rational intervals and a 35-term survival sum encloses G between 0.5799288331138616032330 and 0.5799288331138616032368; the squared tail is bounded by 3.772×10⁻²¹. This independently certifies the wider frozen decimal bracket without treating ordinary rounded Decimal arithmetic alone as a certificate.
residual_risks: Fixed points of the Poisson mean-field map only; no claim of nonlinear global convergence, finite-population equilibrium, or all-mean Gini ordering.

value.rationale: Correcting the original inequality claim and obtaining the exact mean-one benchmark would be useful, but the earlier revised paper already does both. The residual general-mean formulas amount to standard queue moments and the inversion of one quadratic; the improved decimal certificate is not motivated by any decision near the Gini gap, which is already separated using the first survival term. No independently worthwhile unresolved target remains as framed.
residual_risks: This does not rule out substantively different work on convergence, finite-population limits, or all-mean inequality orders.
